title: Show which plates to load for the weight you're about to lift
problem: Between sets of a barbell lift, the app shows a total like 185 lbs, and you work out in your head, or on the phone's calculator, which plates go on each side of a 45 lb bar. It is a small sum, but it comes up on every warm-up and weight change.

evidence.quote_or_summary: 6 thumbs-up: "I think a plate calculator similar to what Hevy has would be very useful." The request includes a starting weight for the bar or machine.
LiftLog user's three requests start with a plate calculator: "to save having to use phone calculator."
User asks for a configurable bar weight because "its harder to remember what those weigh"; the maintainer closed it as covered by the plate-calculator request.
The app today: a logged set shows only its total weight in lbs; there is no bar weight or plate breakdown anywhere in src/.

hypothesis: If the log panel shows the plates per side for the current weight of a barbell lift, the owner would load the bar without doing the sum, on every warm-up and weight change.
acceptance_criteria: For exercises marked as barbell (default for GZCLP T1 and T2 lifts; a toggle per exercise), the log panel shows plates per side under the weight box, for example '185 = bar 45 + 45, 25 per side'
Bar weight (default 45 lbs) and available plates (default 45, 35, 25, 10, 5, 2.5) are set once in settings and kept in synced settings
A weight that can't be made with the available plates says so and shows the nearest loadable weights either side
Updates as the weight changes (prefill, +/- steps, typing); bodyweight sets (weight 0) show nothing
Unit tests for the plate breakdown in src/utils/__tests__; a Playwright check in anonymous mode; settings sync is the only touch on the stored format
success_signal: Over two weeks the owner loads the bar from the on-screen breakdown and stops doing plate sums between sets.
strongest_reason_not_to_build: Experienced lifters do plate math without thinking, the owner has never asked for it, and the evidence is from one other tracker's users; it saves seconds, not planning.
